title: Improve a text with AI
prompt:
# Story: Improve a text with AI

- **Story**: XXX-improve-with-ai
- **Created**: 2026-11-03
- **Status**: Draft

## Story

As a team member, I want an "Improve with AI" button in the dialog where I edit a principle that asks the AI for a clearer
text and lets me use its proposal, so that I write better principles without leaving the dialog. The same button must be usable
in any other dialog or screen that edits a text.

## Acceptance tests

The button in the Edit principle dialog

- [ ] **Given** the Edit principle dialog, **Then** a collapsed "Improve with AI" button shows under the Description.
- [ ] **Given** the button, **When** the user presses it, **Then** a panel opens with the title "Improve with AI", a Hide (X)
  button, four quick actions ("Improve this", "Make it actionable", "Ask me questions", "Shorten"), a field with the
  placeholder "Ask for a change, for example: focus on security", and a Send button that is disabled while the field is empty.
- [ ] **Given** the user hides the panel and opens it again, **Then** the conversation and what was typed in the dialog are still there.

Asking and using the answer

- [ ] **Given** the panel, **When** the user presses "Shorten", **Then** it shows as the user's message, "Thinking..." shows until
  the first text arrives, the reply streams in, and every quick action is disabled until it ends.
- [ ] **Given** the user types "focus on security" and presses Enter, **Then** the instruction is sent, and the dialog is not
  submitted.
- [ ] **Given** a reply with new text, **Then** it shows a short comment and a "Proposed text" card with a "Use this text" button.
- [ ] **Given** a proposal, **When** the user presses "Use this text", **Then** it replaces the Description only, not the Name, the
  button reads "In the editor" and is disabled, and nothing is saved until the user presses Save.
- [ ] **Given** a reply that is still streaming, or was cut off, **Then** "Use this text" is disabled, and a cut-off one says
  "Incomplete, so it cannot be used."
- [ ] **Given** a reply is streaming, **When** the user presses Stop, **Then** the text received so far stays, it cannot be used,
  and Send comes back.
- [ ] **Given** a reply, **Then** a line shows its tokens: input, output, cache read and cache write.

When the request fails

- [ ] **Given** the backend cannot be reached or answers with an error, **Then** the error shows with a Retry button, and Retry
  sends the last instruction again without adding a second user message.
- [ ] **Given** no model is connected for the project, **Then** the error says so and where to connect it ("Connect the model in
  Integrations.").

The connection to the model goes through the backend

- [ ] **Given** the user asks for an improvement, **Then** the browser calls only the BWYN backend over its REST API. It never
  calls the model provider, and no key or token is in the bundle or in any response to the browser.
- [ ] **Given** the call, **Then** it carries the project, the instruction, the conversation so far, and the name and the text as
  they are in the dialog right now. The reply comes back as a stream of text, then the usage, then the end, or an error.
- [ ] **Given** a project with no connection to the model, **Then** the backend answers with a clear error status and a message, and
  does not call the model.
- [ ] **Given** the user closes the dialog while a reply streams, **Then** the call is cancelled and the backend stops asking the model.
- [ ] **Given** the backend, **Then** this API is described in its OpenAPI document.

The button is reusable

- [ ] **Given** a second screen (the Drivers dialog) that uses the button with its own noun "driver", its own quick actions and its
  own instructions, **Then** the panel shows those quick actions, the proposal replaces that screen's text, and nothing of the
  principle dialog is shown.
- [ ] **Given** two dialogs that use the button, **Then** each keeps its own conversation, and neither sees the other's.
- [ ] **Given** a screen that uses the button, **Then** it only gives the button what it needs (the project, the current text, the
  noun, the quick actions, the instructions for the AI and what to do with a proposal). The button does not know about principles.

## Business rules and constraints

- The AI only suggests. It never saves, and it never changes the Name.
- The reply has a short comment (at most three sentences, or at most three short questions) and, only when the AI proposes new text, the
  proposed text.
- The AI keeps the user's intent, language and facts, invents nothing, and prefers plain, specific, positive wording. It never
  contradicts a non-negotiable practice. If the text does, its comment says so.
- The AI is given, as stable (cached) context, the practices and the other principles of the project, never the one being edited. The
  name and the text as they are in the dialog travel with each instruction.
- The conversation belongs to the open dialog and is lost when it closes.
- The keys of the model stay on the backend. Every project has its own connection to the model, set in Integrations.
- The button and the panel are one shared component. What is specific to a screen (instructions, context, quick actions, noun) is given
  by that screen, never written inside the component.
- Before this story the button called a dev server directly. That call is replaced, not kept next to the new one.

## Out of scope

- Putting the button in other screens (Drivers, ADRs, Architecture): each is its own story. This story proves it can be reused with a
  second, test screen only.
- Connecting the model, and the token totals of a project (Integrations).
- Keeping the conversation after the dialog closes, and choosing the model in the dialog.

## Tasks

- [ ] Describe the REST call for the assistant in the OpenAPI document: request, streamed reply, usage, end and error.
- [ ] Add the backend endpoint that checks the project's connection, calls the model with the context cached, and streams the reply.
- [ ] Return a clear error when the project has no connection, and stop the model call when the browser cancels.
- [ ] Replace the direct dev-server call in the frontend with a client of the backend REST API, with the same stream of text, usage and end.
- [ ] Turn the button and its panel into one shared component that gets the project, text, noun, quick actions, instructions and what to
  do with a proposal from the screen using it.
- [ ] Use the shared component in the Edit principle dialog, passing the principle's instructions, quick actions and context.
- [ ] Use the shared component in one more screen in a test, to prove that nothing of the principle dialog leaks into it.

---

# Reference

Spike: `bwyn-frontend/spikes/home-page/DriverAssistant.tsx` (the button and the panel), `useDriverAssistant.ts` (the conversation),
`builder/bedrockClient.ts` (today's call to the dev server `/api/draft`) and `server/bedrock.js` (the dev server that keeps the keys).
The principle's instructions and quick actions are in `principlePrompts.ts`. The backend is Spring Boot (ADR 0004) and documents its
API with OpenAPI (ADR 0010).


There is no need for Query/Command, You can directly create an ApplicationService with the correct prefix for the use case here, you decide the best one.

This new *ApplicatioService application (use case) class is the layer in between the rest api and the outbound (going to the LLM).

as task make this component as a reusable component
